mappings.note: The essay's governing idea -- the bond between person and country. C-1.1-LO-23.
Why Swami Ramtirth was charmed by the fruit-seller's reply -- the youth asked only that Japan be well spoken of. A private act with a national effect, C-1.1-LO-26.
What the Japanese youth asked as payment and what he seems like -- the same private-act-national-effect point, C-1.1-LO-26.
Arguments for not holding oneself apart from one's country -- C-1.1-LO-23 asks exactly for the writer's reasoning on that bond.
That a country's disgrace and glory pass to the citizen and back -- the inseparability, C-1.1-LO-23.
What the word 'daraar' in 'a crack appeared in this wall of joy' points to. A figurative reading, so the style-and-image competency C-1.2.

Which kind of questions the writer enjoys answering -- those that open a subject out. It bears on the essay's question-and-answer method, C-1.2. NOTE: the stem is cut off mid-sentence and its options have slipped into the answer field; it duplicates the next item.
The same question in intact MCQ form -- the essay's prashnottar manner, C-1.2.
Why the days of subjection are called 'deen' -- self-respect was crushed. The shame-of-subjection outcome C-1.1-LO-24.
Means cannot give a man pride if his country is in bondage -- C-1.1-LO-24.
Which two things the 'gaanth' ties -- country and citizen. C-1.1-LO-23.
What you and yours do to keep public and historic places clean and handsome: C-1.1-LO-25 for the civic duty, C-4.3-LO-14 because the question is framed on the essay's saundarya-bodh.
What to do and not do so the country's honour is not dented -- the duties of a citizen, C-1.1-LO-25.
Frame three questions on the given passage. C-4.1 for the language work of forming questions; C-1.2 because the task is modelled on the essay's own prashnottar structure.
Hold a discussion on 'a country is not merely a stretch of territory' and report it: C-2.1 for the reasoned discussion, C-1.1-LO-23 for the proposition being argued.

The word 'desh' across Eighth Schedule languages plus the sentence in your mother tongue -- Indian linguistic diversity, C-4.3 at competency level and CG-4. None of LO-12, LO-13 or LO-14 covers a multilingual word list.
Who wrote the essay. Authorship recall, stated by no LO here, so C-1.1 at competency level.
Identify further features like the question-and-answer structure -- style analysis, C-1.2.
Choose which of the listed titles you would write an essay on, and why -- composition and its planning, C-2.2.
What goes on in your area when an election begins -- the voting outcome C-1.1-LO-26.

DEFECT: the stem 'so that this does not happen, what can be done?' has lost its antecedent; the answer shows it is about damage to library books. Mapped on that basis to the duties-of-a-citizen outcome C-1.1-LO-25.
Which library rules you keep and why keeping them is obligatory -- duties as the counterpart of rights, C-1.1-LO-25.
Write to the headmaster asking for Braille books for blind classmates -- letter writing, C-2.2.
Compose a vote of thanks to soldiers, teachers, farmers, workers, artists and scientists: C-2.2 for the composition, C-4.3-LO-12 for the desh-gaurav it is meant to express.
Design an advertisement urging people to vote for the right candidate: LO-26 for the voting message, C-2.2 for the composing.
Which other habits injure the country's beauty, after the banana-peel passage: C-4.3-LO-14 for the saundarya-bodh, C-1.1-LO-25 for the civic duty at stake.
Statements on the essay's main ideas -- a person's completeness reaches out to the nation, and the two honours are bound together. C-1.1-LO-23.
The rays of tejasvita in Lala Lajpat Rai's pen and speech -- a passage the essay uses to kindle desh-gaurav, C-4.3-LO-12.
Whose the two little stories were -- episodes from two young men's lives. They carry the private-act-national-effect argument, C-1.1-LO-26.
The best description of the essay's manner -- question-and-answer, conversational. Style, C-1.2.
The year Prabhakar died. Biographical recall, no LO states it, so C-1.1.
That gifts and means cannot confer pride on a man of an enslaved country: LO-23 for the inseparability the answer names, LO-24 for the shame of subjection it rests on.
Fill in: we cannot succeed until we grasp our country's 'bheetari' condition -- the inner condition the essay then unpacks as shakti-bodh and saundarya-bodh, C-4.3-LO-14.
The order in which a person's completeness widens -- home, neighbourhood, town, country. C-1.1-LO-23.
Explain how the word 'bhookamp' is used in context -- a figurative usage, C-1.2.
Why he insists on grasping the country's inner condition, and what shakti-bodh and saundarya-bodh mean -- C-4.3-LO-14 names both.
Compare the Ramtirth episode with the foreign student and the Japanese library -- both show a single act telling on a nation, C-1.1-LO-26.
The aptness of the title and the essay's central idea -- the person-and-country bond, C-1.1-LO-23.
Prove from the two Japanese episodes that a citizen's conduct mirrors his country -- C-1.1-LO-26.
The Kemal Pasha and Nehru episodes on 'bhavana ki mahatta' and able leadership -- C-4.3-LO-13 is the greatness-of-feeling outcome by name.
Why shakti-bodh and saundarya-bodh are called the country's two basic needs, and their relevance now -- C-4.3-LO-14.
Analyse the language and style and the use of the conversational manner -- C-1.2.
The writer's idea of the ideal citizen -- duties and rights together, C-1.1-LO-25.
